description: Read the v=MCPv1 TXT records at a domain, the keys the MCP Registry DNS login (mcp-publisher login dns) verifies a signature against, and judge each the way the registry does: v=MCPv1; k=<algorithm>; p=<key> in that order and case, k exactly ed25519 or ecdsap384, p padded standard base64 of a 32-byte ed25519 key or a 49-byte compressed P-384 point that lies on the curve. `verdict` is not_configured (info), valid (every record usable, pass), some_invalid (warn), invalid (none usable, fail) or misplaced (fail: no usable record at the domain, but one at _mcp-auth. or _mcp-registry., which the registry never reads; MCP_KEYS_MISPLACED, analysis.misplaced); no grade. Each problem is a warn finding whose title names the key: MCP_KEYS_RECORD_IGNORED, MCP_KEYS_UNKNOWN_ALGORITHM, MCP_KEYS_KEY_NOT_BASE64, MCP_KEYS_KEY_WRONG_LENGTH, MCP_KEYS_ECDSA_NOT_COMPRESSED, MCP_KEYS_ECDSA_NOT_ON_CURVE. MCP_KEYS_NO_VALID_KEY (error) means the login will fail; MCP_KEYS_NO_RECORD (info) means there is no record, and many hosted MCP servers use OAuth instead. `analysis.keys[]` carries algorithm, key length and SHA-256 fingerprint per record; `analysis.apex` names the registrable domain when the input was a subdomain. Read-only.

domain.description: Apex domain to inspect, e.g. "google.com". No scheme, no path.
